I've seen many stats for who is and isn't going to win, but each time it looks like it wasn't done right. So, who actually has done a good survey to see who is going to win? One that's independent from both sides?
What are the actual statistics for the election?

There's no such thing as "done right" because the right method is whichever method most accurately predicts the outcome. You don't know which method that was until you know the outcome.

There's polling and then there's forecasting. Polling is more like just accumulating data and then you present whatever you end up with. You don't take on the role of assigning meaning to the data you collect. Forecasting is like using data from a survey taken along with the poll and analyzing and manipulating it in a way to attempt to make it predict an outcome.

The difficulty is that the line is blurred. The dumbass msm takes raw data and presents it as if it's predictive. The politically motivated pretend to be accumulating "raw data" but selects parameters that they know will favor their preferred politics. Statisticians and forecasters will take the data and try to interpret it by weighting the data according to other factors. Let's say there's a poll and the results are 45 support Purple and 53 support Orange, and the survey says that 28% of respondents were registered Purples and 34% were registered Oranges. The results are predictive if the district really has 28% and 34% registered purples and oranges, but if the district is actually 37% purples and 32% organges, then purples will cry "Bias!" A forecaster might count each response given by a purple as worth 1.32 responses, and each response by an orange as only .94 of a response, then the orange supporters will cry "Bias!"

What if the forecaster weights turnout according to what the turnout was in 2014, then people will cry bias becuase the demographic shifts of a different electorate will make people cry bias. There's all sorts of shit like that. That's why the best method seems to be to just aggregate multiple polls and pull your answer that way. It's like askin a thousand people how many jelly beans are in a jar. A lot of people will be way off, but the average of tall the wrong answeres will giv you a pretty solid answer for what it actually is. You just total up the polls and average them out.
